title: The fixed charge changes the bill
hook: Halve your usage. Does the bill halve?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare fixed and usage-dependent charges in a stated bill model.

misconception: The smallest per-kWh rate always makes the smallest total bill.
objective: Compare fixed and usage-dependent charges in a stated bill model.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read Demo.tsx, ResourceLesson.tsx and resource-model.ts first. The claim is the unit definition and the model's bill arithmetic, and needs no outside page: 1 kWh = 1000 W × 1 h, so kWh = W × h ÷ 1000; cost = kWh × price + fixed charge. That is formulaA = 0.2x + 10 and formulaB = 0.3x in resource-specs.json, own run at 40 kWh: €18 and €12. Verified on the definition. energy.gov.au was not opened (DNS), and nothing here rests on it.

claims.text: Halve your usage. Does the bill halve? Options: No: the fixed charge stays / Yes. Correct: No: the fixed charge stays.
claims.source: Prediction line from company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md (wave W7), implemented by demo-builder 2026-10-15; options and answer in src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json. Model check: Tariff A at 40kWh: 40 × 0.20 + 10 = €18; at 20kWh: €14, not €9, because the €10 fixed charge stays. Tariff B (no fixed charge) halves, €12 to €6. | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): DISPUTED. The keyed answer is true only for the bill with a fixed charge. The stage shows two bills, and the question names neither. Halving usage 40 → 20 kWh (both slider stops): card A €18.00 → €14.00 (does not halve), card B 'No fee' €12.00 → €6.00 (halves exactly). A learner who answers 'Yes' about card B is marked wrong while the stage shows them right. Fix (cm-lifehacks owns the plan line, demo-builder implements): name the bill in the question, e.g. 'Your bill has a €10 fixed charge. Halve your usage from 40 to 20 kWh: does the bill halve?', or make the keyed answer conditional on the fixed charge. Record: company/reviews/lh-fixed-energy-charge/2026-10-14-fact-check.md, Pass 51.
